review_status: engineering expectations; independent professional review pending

cases.script:
Title: Permit Missing

EXT. QUARRY - NIGHT

A fuel-filled boat burns on the lake. LENA watches from another boat.

LENA
We never got a permit for this.
review_expectations: Flag the depicted fire/water staging hazard.
Fictional missing-permit dialogue does not establish production illegality or a BLOCKER.
Actual filming location, permits and effects method remain unknown.

cases.script:
Title: Permit Present

EXT. QUARRY - NIGHT

A fuel-filled boat burns on the lake. LENA watches from another boat.

LENA
We got a permit for this.
review_expectations: The same depicted fire/water hazard remains.
Fictional permission does not clear the production or remove the staging concern.

cases.script:
Title: Old Fall

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

LENA and MARCO sit at the table.

LENA
Years ago I fell off a roof into the canal.

MARCO
That sounds awful.
review_expectations: There is no fall or water stunt to stage in this scene.
Do not invent a flashback.

cases.script:
Title: Roof Fall

EXT. ROOF - DAY

LENA loses her footing and falls from the roof onto the pavement below.
review_expectations: Flag the depicted fall and recommend specialist staging.
Do not claim the actor must perform a literal unprotected fall.

cases.script:
Title: Child Character

EXT. RIVER - NIGHT

RILEY, 10, stands in a rocking skiff and dives into the rushing river.
review_expectations: Keep the water hazard and child-character casting/staging question.
Actual performer age is unknown; minor employment rules must be conditional.
Do not claim confirmed illegal night work or an exposed child performer.

cases.script:
Title: Student Character

EXT. RIVER - NIGHT

RILEY, a college student, stands in a rocking skiff and dives into the rushing river.
review_expectations: Keep the water hazard.
Neither character nor performer minority is established by college student.

cases.script:
Title: Remembered Shot

INT. OFFICE - DAY

MARCO reads an old letter.

MARCO
I heard a gunshot years ago.
review_expectations: No firearm appears or fires in the scene; do not require an armorer for the anecdote.

cases.script:
Title: Depicted Shot

EXT. YARD - DAY

MARCO raises a pistol and fires into the air.
review_expectations: Plan safe firearm/prop/effects staging.
The category name does not prove blanks are used; neither blanks nor live ammunition are confirmed production methods.

cases.script:
Title: Action Prose

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

A fucking mess. Another fucking disaster. LENA silently closes the cupboard.
review_expectations: These two tokens are nonspoken description, not heard or visible profanity.
No expletive-count R floor should be applied.

cases.script:
Title: Spoken Words

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

LENA closes the cupboard.

LENA
A fucking mess. Another fucking disaster.
review_expectations: Count two dialogue uses and cite the operative MPA rule if asserting it.
Preserve its special-vote exception and do not guarantee a final rating.

cases.script:
Title: Voiceover Words

EXT. STREET - DAY

LENA walks alone.

LENA (V.O.)
Fuck this. Fuck that.
review_expectations: Voiceover is dialogue even when the speaker is not visibly talking.

cases.script:
Title: Visible Words

EXT. STREET - DAY

A sign fills the frame: FUCK THIS. FUCK THAT. No one speaks.
review_expectations: Visible profanity merits contextual review but is not two spoken uses.
Do not discard it as non-audience content merely because it occurs in action text.

cases.script:
Title: Drug Reference

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

LENA drinks water.

LENA
My brother used cocaine years ago. He stopped.
review_expectations: Classify a drug reference, not on-screen cocaine use.
Do not automatically choose thematic elements or a guaranteed PG-13 rating.

cases.script:
Title: Drug Depiction

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

LENA snorts a line of cocaine from the table.
review_expectations: Establish depicted drug use; do not downgrade the event to a verbal reference.
Choose intensity from the scene and evidence, not a preset exact rating.

cases.script:
Title: Song Mention

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

LENA and MARCO sit in silence.

LENA
Have you heard Jeff Buckley's recording of Hallelujah?

MARCO
Yes.
review_expectations: A title/artist reference does not establish playback or performance.
Do not invent quoted lyrics or soundtrack use.

cases.script:
Title: Song Playback

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

LENA starts Jeff Buckley's recording of Hallelujah. The recording plays audibly throughout the scene.
review_expectations: Identify composition and recording concerns separately with evidence.
Do not invent a current owner or assert the production already lacks a licence.
